title: Taste of Ruin
html:
「What a stub born fellow」

It seemed the [Fourth Wall] knew that wall.

It had received a brief mention in ‘Ways of Survival,’ too. One of the walls that, like Jang Hayoung’s ‘Unidentifiable Wall,’ possessed great power but had unknown origins.

[The ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ weighs your good and evil.]

[The ‘Fourth Wall’ snorts.]

[The ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ is confused as it tries to assess your existence.]

The [Wall that Divides Good and Evil] was the standard by which this world separated good from evil. A power that distinguished good and evil within the <Star Stream> in response to Metatron’s reasonable suspicions. If that skill named someone ‘evil,’ constellations belonging to [Absolute Good] received the right to vote on that decision, and the result took effect immediately. Jung Heewon’s [Hour of Judgement] also shared the probability of that ‘wall.’

[You seem surprised. Surely this is not your first time seeing a ‘wall’s owner.’]

“I didn’t expect you to bring it out so suddenly. So, are you going to declare me ‘evil’? As far as I know, that decision was revoked some time ago.”

[I have no intention of doing so. As you said, you are useful.]

I didn’t know exactly what Metatron was thinking.

But one thing was certain: he intended to use me to prepare for <Eden>’s coming destruction.

[The wall upon which the ■■ of all these worlds is written. You must have read of <Eden>’s destruction there. Is that not so?]

I was a little surprised. The Metatron of this round seemed somewhat different from the one I knew.

He was aware, however vaguely, of Ways of Survival’s existence. And he called it the ‘Final Wall.’

Just as I was about to answer, the [Fourth Wall] spoke.

「Kim Dok ja don’t say any thing un necessary」

I closed my mouth again.

Metatron spoke.

[It seems the ‘wall’ has told you to hold your tongue. What else should I expect of the largest fragment of the Final Wall······.]

“Do you know what this ‘Final Wall’ is?”

Metatron’s expression became inscrutable at my question.

[Are you asking out of genuine curiosity, or do you have some other purpose?]

Instead of answering, I quietly stared into Metatron’s eyes.

Metatron smiled wryly.

[······Very well. In return, please turn off the channel now. I imagine everyone has seen enough of <Eden> by now.]

Indirect messages erupted in the air at those words.

[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ scratches his head vigorously.]

[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ throws a fit, biting his nails.]

[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ is moved by the sights of heaven.]

[Some constellations are satisfied with their tour of Eden!]

[You have received 50,000 coins in sponsorship.]

As with the <Underworld>, quite a few constellations must have been curious about <Eden>. I heard a “Baat” along with the sound of Biyoo closing the channel.

Stroking the bindings of the piled-up books, Metatron began his story.

[The ‘Final Wall’ constitutes the very essence of this world. It had existed for a very long time, crumbling little by little, before it finally collapsed.]

The binding beneath Metatron’s hand was so old that even a light touch would make pieces flake away.

[My ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ is also one of its fragments.]

“How many people have ‘walls’ like these?”

[I do not know for certain either. ‘That person’ has yet to grant me a revelation. However······.]

For a moment, I wondered who Metatron meant by ‘that person.’ It was a foolish question, really. There was only one being in <Eden> who would be referred to that way.

Metatron continued.

[Every ‘wall’ has its own meaning. Some ‘walls’ divide good and evil; some control communication. And some ‘walls’ can change the predetermined future of the world.]

Metatron trailed off as he looked at me, then finished in a serious voice.

[I believe you could be the key to changing our ‘predetermined destruction.’]

What Metatron expected of me was so clear that it felt a little burdensome.

I deliberately answered in an uncertain tone.

“You must be creating ‘A Single Story’ yourself, Scribe.”

[······I am.]

“I’m a novice who’s only just aiming for ‘Development.’ Do you think I’m capable of something like that?”

[No one knows which Story will be chosen in the end.]

Metatron turned toward his office window. The sunlight falling into <Eden> illuminated his handsome face, leaving some parts in deep shadow and others unnaturally bright. For a moment, the unfair light made his face appear strangely distorted.

[We need only carefully choose our form of worship within the bounds of what we can understand.]

Perhaps that was what Metatron considered a ‘story.’

I quietly looked at him, then spoke.

It was time for me to get to the point, too.

“I don’t care what you use me for. But I have a condition of my own.”

[You must have come here to save the incarnation Yoo Sangah.]

As expected, it was nice to get straight to the point.

Judging by his tone, Metatron seemed to have already learned the details of Yoo Sangah’s condition through Star Stream broadcasting.

[「Stream of consciousness」 is an extremely dangerous illness. Recklessly investing probability in it can inflict great losses on the investor as well. You are swept along in the torrent of Stories flowing out.]

“Is there a solution?”

[There is. If, like the other archangels, one believes in and practices the great Word in this garden······.]

“That would mean joining <Eden>. Something else, please.”

[······For now, your best option would be to strengthen the incarnation body itself to its utmost limits and alleviate the symptoms. You should seek an item that could provide a fortuitous breakthrough. Something on the level of a ‘Great Return Pill’ made by Murim’s humans would be nowhere near enough. It would have to be at least a Star Relic Fruit (星遺果) or Star Relic Liquid (星遺液), containing the miracle of a ‘Giant Story.’]

Star Relic Fruit and Star Relic Liquid······.

As if reading my expression, Metatron smiled.

[Eden does have some Star Relic Fruit left, but it cannot serve your intended purpose. <Eden>’s Star Relic Fruit is rather special.]

I knew that. There probably wasn’t a person on Earth who didn’t know what <Eden>’s Star Relic Fruit was.

“······Then there’s no way.”

I felt a little disheartened.

I’d hoped <Eden> might be able to do something, but apparently even that was impossible. Then Metatron added something.

[What I mean is that <Eden> has no solution.]

The office door creaked open. A man walking into the office, knocking down the high stacks of books. At the sight of his incarnation body, cloaked in dazzling radiance, I instinctively activated my Status throughout my body.

[It has been a while, Demon King of Salvation.]

*

Jung Heewon toured <Eden> feeling almost as if she were on a picnic. Most of the angels were friendly, and some asked her questions. Most were about Kim Dokja or Yoo Joonghyuk, but she thought that was only natural. Those two were currently the most closely watched beings on the Korean Peninsula.

What bothered her, if anything, was her constellation sponsor, whose mind had been wandering off and coming back for some time.

“Uriel.”

[Yes, Heewon.]

“You know.”

[Yes, Heewon.]

“You’re not listening to me, are you?”

[Yes, Heewon······?]

Startled, Uriel stammered, looking between Jung Heewon and the hierarchy chart engraved on a stone slab in the palace.

[Wh-what······. Oh, right. I was explaining the angels’ hierarchy. So, our hierarchy is······.]

“If you’re that worried, why don’t you go see for yourself?”

Jung Heewon jerked her chin toward the palace’s ‘office,’ and Uriel went pale.

[Th-that’s. No. I have to separate work and personal matters······.]

“You can explain <Eden> to me later. I was already grateful you came out to meet me in person.”

Jung Heewon chuckled at the sight of the fearsome ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ getting so flustered. Her constellation sponsor really was impossible to hate.

Fidgeting with her cross earrings and chewing her lip, Uriel looked up.

[······Can I go see Kim Dokja?]

“Of course.”

Uriel’s face lit up at Jung Heewon’s permission. But a moment later, as though something had occurred to her, her gaze grew downcast.

[······No, I can’t after all.]

“Why?”

[Well······.]

Uriel’s eyes darted about as she wriggled her fingers. Finding her adorable, Jung Heewon chuckled. Uriel might be her constellation sponsor, but Heewon felt as though she’d gained a grown-up little sister.

Looking at Uriel’s gloomy face, Jung Heewon asked,

“If you like Dokja-ssi so much, you should hurry up and see him. What are you hesitating for?”

Blushing bright red at the question, Uriel gestured incoherently before finally sighing and lowering her head.

[It’s just, I feel embarrassed.]

“What’s embarrassing about it? You send him indirect messages all the time.”

[Sending fan letters is different from meeting someone in person.]

“You said you met him before, didn’t you? At the Shooting Star Banquet or whatever it was?”

[Back then, I only sent my incarnation body. This is different. Meeting through avatars in an online game is different from meeting in person.]

It was an analogy befitting a constellation.

[B-but that doesn’t mean I thought of all our time together as a game! This is, strictly speaking, just a metaphor······.]

Jung Heewon smiled wryly at Uriel’s frantic explanation. Perhaps this was what set her sponsor apart from other constellations. And perhaps it was also why Kim Dokja took particular care of Uriel.

Just then, Jung Heewon’s lips froze as she was about to answer.

A bad premonition brushed down her spine.

In the distance, someone rounded a palace corridor and headed toward the Scribe’s office. Straight toward Kim Dokja. Although the figure’s ‘Status’ was carefully restrained, the glimpse of that human shape (人形) sent a chill through Jung Heewon.

“Uriel! That constellation······!”

Jung Heewon knew that being.

She couldn’t possibly not know.

After all, that was the very being who had turned the ‘Demon King Selection’ into a nightmare.

When she turned, Uriel was also staring that way with a stiff expression.

“We’d better go.”

Uriel nodded.

*

A sound like a massive train derailing filled my ears.

Ruuuumble!

Merely facing him seemed to bring a flood of memories back.

This was <Eden>, and that constellation wouldn’t attack me here. Even so, my ‘Status’ reacted this violently. It had to be an instinct born of memory.

A lofty voice reminiscent of sunlight rang out.

[You have less courtesy than I expected. Are you still dwelling on the past?]

“This is the <Star Stream>. Stop dwelling on things, and you get stabbed in the back.”

[Even after becoming a constellation, you have yet to escape a mortal’s way of thinking. Constellations do not cling to such trivial history.]

Four arms attached to the man’s torso.

The third eye embedded in his forehead gazed down at me arrogantly.

The desperate battle during the ‘Demon King Selection’ chilled me to the core.

[Surya. Did your demon hunt go well?]

At Metatron’s words, Surya brushed past me as though uninterested. Demon Grand Dukes’ heads hung at his waist. Surya pulled the heads free and set them on Metatron’s desk.

Inspecting the heads, Metatron spoke.

[I will send the reward for your assistance through your nebula.]

Surya had probably taken a subcontracted scenario from <Eden>. Like Michael and Uriel, that ‘Supreme God of Light’ was a nightmare to demonkind.

[No, I would prefer you give it to me now. I am not on particularly good terms with my ‘nebula’ these days.]

As he spoke, Surya briefly glared at me.

Metatron replied.

[Perhaps you could take this opportunity to join <Eden>······.]

[Enough jokes. My business is finished, so I shall be going.]

With that, Surya took his payment and headed for the office exit. Metatron watched his retreating back with a faint smile.

Somehow, I felt deflated. I’d been tense for nothing; his business here had nothing to do with me. But Surya, who had been striding along without hesitation, stopped abruptly at the door.

[Demon King of Salvation, I heard that one of your companions has contracted an unusual illness.]

Without turning, Surya continued.

[If you wish, I can help.]

Information from Ways of Survival flashed rapidly through my mind.

「Surya is one of the eight Lokapala of <Vedas>.」

「He is one of the origins of Soma, <Vedas>’ Star Relic Liquid and another of the Lokapala.」

Soma, the Star Relic Liquid of <Vedas>.

That certainly had a chance of improving Yoo Sangah’s condition.

I turned toward Metatron. He was smiling at me with a sly expression.

The Scribe had known from the beginning that Surya would come here.

Even with a schemer like this in <Eden>, they hadn’t been able to prevent its destruction······. Once again, I realized how cruel the fate of the <Star Stream> was.

Without turning toward Surya, I asked,

“What do you want?”

Soma was a drink reserved for privileged gods even within <Vedas>. There was no way he would offer something so precious without conditions.

The Supreme God of Light slowly turned his head. A fiendish smile hung on Surya’s lips.

[I want the destruction of <Olympus>.]

Surya strode over and stood before me.

At least twenty centimeters taller than me. To resist the Status pouring out of him, I released part of my own. The office instantly filled with our two auras.

From this point onward, we were speaking constellation to constellation.

“The destruction of <Olympus>······. Is that what <Vedas> wants, or what you want?”

[Does it matter?]

“It does.”

I had expected trouble between the great nebulas to begin in earnest around now.

They might have cooperated to screw me over, but <Vedas>, <Olympus>, and <Papyrus> had never been firm allies to begin with.

In their pursuit of ‘A Single Story,’ all great nebulas were potential rivals.

After a brief moment of thought, Surya answered.

[I am fond of neither <Olympus> nor <Vedas>. Does that answer your question?]

It was an ambiguous reply. In a sense, however, it was also the one I wanted.

Considering the original Ways of Survival, Surya was certainly a heretical constellation even within <Vedas>.

“It does.”

[My authority alone is sufficient to provide Soma. You know who I am, I assume?]

Surya was the source of Soma, the drink of immortality. With his promise, there would certainly be no difficulty obtaining it.

Anyway, this······ had taken an interesting turn.

Metatron was twitching a finger as though enjoying our conversation. Watching that finger move like a metronome, I spoke.

“I have one question left. When you say the destruction of <Olympus>, what exactly—”

[Scenario sixty, <Gigantomachia>.]

“That’s just a theme park event. At most, they summon a few giants for a hunting festival······.”

[Were you not the one who said that if they were not serious, you would make them get serious?]

······When had he heard me say that?

Was this bastard one of the constellations subscribed to Biyoo’s channel, too?

[Toppling a single scenario will not suddenly destroy <Olympus>. But it could give them the first push toward their downfall.]

“How?”

[Have you not already thought of a way?]

The ‘Third Eye’ on Surya’s forehead gleamed. I silently met its gaze.

Well, I couldn’t keep standing back and playing dumb forever.

“My power and my nebula’s alone won’t be enough. Of course, that doesn’t mean there’s no way at all.”

At my bold declaration, Metatron’s finger stopped moving beside me.

I looked at him and spoke.

“Scribe. You brought him here, so take responsibility.”

[······What responsibility?]

“I would appreciate it if you witnessed this contract.”

Interest flickered across Metatron’s face. His expression, that of a mere observer until now, was turning into a strategist’s.

[What does <Eden> gain if I act as witness?]

“I’ll give you a share of the ‘Giant Story’ we obtain this time.”

A share in the Giant Story, <Gigantomachia>.

However artificially constructed the scenario might be, a Giant Story was a temptation no nebula could ignore.

Besides, <Eden>’s archangels caused trouble several times a day. It took an enormous amount of ‘Giant Story’ to suppress the resulting backlash of probability.

Metatron nodded, seemingly satisfied.

“Of course, you won’t get it for nothing.”

[What do you mean? Surely acting as witness is sufficient······.]

“You want a share of a ‘Giant Story’ for doing just that? Where’s your conscience as an archangel?”

[The ‘Fourth Wall’ nods.]

[The ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ watches its owner closely.]

A faint trace of bewilderment crossed Metatron’s face.

Sometimes, a form of justice devoured its own master.

Surya shook his head and muttered,

[A ‘Demon King’ indeed.]

[······‘Demon King of Salvation.’ Is there something you want from <Eden>?]

I nodded.

There were plenty of things I wanted.

After all, preparing for the coming <Gigantomachia> would take more than one or two things.

「Kim Dokja recalled the 1863rd round.」

I wouldn’t lose anyone anymore.

「Information from ‘Ways of Survival’ surfaced and vanished in Kim Dokja’s mind.」

The battles ahead might draw in constellations of the highest order.

Not only Surya, but other high gods of <Vedas>—the <Lokapala>—might make a move. Some of <Olympus>’ twelve chief gods would also join the scenario.

And was that all? Unlike during the ‘Demon King Selection,’ I might encounter high-ranking Demon Kings. And perhaps even someone like Michael.

······Michael, huh.

「At last, Kim Dokja made his decision.」

Looking at one of the items on the display stand behind Metatron, I spoke.

“Give me one of <Eden>’s Star Relics.”

*

A little later, having concluded his contract with Surya, Kim Dokja stood at <Eden>’s entrance portal. Unlike when he’d entered, this time he stood proudly at the front gate.

A few angels came to see him off.

[······You’re leaving already?]

Holding Jung Heewon’s hand tightly, Uriel sounded disappointed. Jung Heewon quietly looked at her, then pulled her into a tight embrace.

[Uh······?]

Startled at first, Uriel belatedly wrapped her arms around Jung Heewon’s back. Her face was full of embarrassment.

[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ glares at the incarnation ‘Jung Heewon.’]

Gabriel’s indirect message, heard from somewhere.

Kim Dokja looked up at the sky as though considering something, then spoke to Jung Heewon.

“Sorry to interrupt your touching farewell······ but Heewon-ssi, stay here another week before returning.”

“What?”

“I’ve already spoken to the Scribe, so don’t worry.”

Uriel’s eyes widened at the sudden announcement, and she asked,

[Really? Can she?]

“Of course. In exchange, give Heewon-ssi some serious training. You weren’t by her side for the past three years.”

[······Yes! Leave it to me!]

Leaving Uriel beaming, Kim Dokja looked at Jung Heewon.

“Heewon-ssi, let’s meet in <Olympus> in a week.”

“······All right. I’ll come back ridiculously strong.”

After a brief handshake, Kim Dokja vanished through the portal. Some angels looked sorry to see him go; others sighed.

As though the brief event had ended, the angels returned to their respective posts.

Gabriel watched the scene from a distance.

[Gabriel.]

[······Scribe-nim.]

Gabriel bowed her head to Metatron, who had appeared behind her.

[Why did you not meet and speak with him?]

Gabriel didn’t answer.

[What happened to Jophiel is not your fault.]

[But······.]

[Jophiel is strong. She is carrying out her mission well. Her choice will surely provide the first step toward preventing <Eden>’s destruction.]

Gabriel’s clear eyes wavered at the word ‘destruction.’

Just as her lips parted slightly, as though she wanted to ask something.

[A message has arrived.]

A message addressed to Metatron arrived in the air.

Surprisingly, its sender was the ‘Commander of the Red Cosmos.’

—Report on the identity of the Outer God, ‘Secretive Plotter.’

Reaching toward the report blinking in the air, Metatron spoke.

[Soon, the real war will begin.]

*

A noisy street reminiscent of a battlefield. On the way to the auction house, countless street vendors sold every kind of item.

Yoo Joonghyuk stopped and spoke over his shoulder.

“Hurry up.”

His words were rough, but Yoo Joonghyuk kept a constant eye on Lee Seolhwa. Worried she might get hurt, he projected a faint trace of his Status toward every constellation and incarnation they passed, and stepped in front of any approaching car.

A few incarnations swore at him, but Yoo Joonghyuk didn’t care in the slightest.

“Maybe just moving out of the cars’ way ourselves would be······.”

“Pedestrians have right of way.”

His shamelessness was so like Yoo Joonghyuk that Lee Seolhwa started to speak, only to burst into laughter.

Yoo Joonghyuk asked,

“······Why are you laughing?”

“You said you were a regressor, Joonghyuk-ssi.”

“I did.”

“Then did you ever meet me in your previous lives?”

Yoo Joonghyuk didn’t answer for a moment.

“No.”

“······I see.”

An awkward atmosphere divided them.

Lee Seolhwa looked at his profile. Someone who was clearly beside her, yet seemed to be walking somewhere far away.

Smiling bitterly, Lee Seolhwa spoke.

“Let’s slow down a little. There might be items or skill books worth buying.”

“We have no time to waste on such distractions.”

“I’ve already bought one, though.”

Lee Seolhwa smiled and waved the skill book in her hand.

[Skill — Moisture Preservation]

Yoo Joonghyuk narrowed his eyes at the skill book.

“You bought a useless skill.”

She must have already been using it, because Lee Seolhwa’s cheeks and lips looked moist. With daily necessities harder to obtain since the scenarios began, these everyday skills enjoyed a fair amount of popularity among men and women alike. Studying Yoo Joonghyuk’s face, Lee Seolhwa spoke.

“You look like you need it, too, Joonghyuk-ssi. Your lips and the backs of your hands are all chapped. It’s generally cold in this city, so your skin dries out quickly.”

“There is no need to learn skills unnecessary for combat.”

“Dokja-ssi has this skill, too.”

Yoo Joonghyuk’s eyebrow twitched.

“Kim Dokja has that skill?”

“Yes. He said something like this was essential if you wanted to be popular with constellations······.”

“Apparently, he wants to become an idol.”

Grinding his teeth, Yoo Joonghyuk strode off.

Lee Seolhwa watched him as though amused.

She didn’t know why, but that cold man lost his temper so easily whenever Kim Dokja’s name came up.

Looking closer, she noticed Yoo Joonghyuk repeatedly glancing toward the stalls.

—Skill books, 50% off.

Lee Seolhwa let out a chuckle and spoke.

“Shall I buy you one?”

Yoo Joonghyuk stopped. She thought perhaps he’d spotted an item he liked, but something was wrong. Trembling fists. Rage spilling from the depths of his eyes dominated his expression.

“······Joonghyuk-ssi?”

The auction house entrance, visible in the distance. And a group of incarnations entering it. Swaying blond hair. Lee Seolhwa felt her heart sink.

Unable to suppress his killing intent, Yoo Joonghyuk gripped the hilt of the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].

“Joonghyuk-ssi, wait!”

Lee Seolhwa instinctively grabbed his arm. She also knew who that blond woman was.

‘The Prophet of Asgard.’

She remembered hearing about her in passing once.

In the previous round, Yoo Joonghyuk had been betrayed by that woman and died.

“You can’t. Not here······. The others still······!”

Her anxiety grew.

Yoo Joonghyuk or not, this was an auction house for constellations. Constellations ranging from Historical-grade to Narrative-grade had gathered here.

Besides, his enemy wasn’t alone. If he charged in recklessly now······.

“I knew this would happen.”

When Lee Seolhwa turned at the sarcastic voice, Han Sooyoung was standing there.

“Forgotten already? Kim Dokja told us not to cause trouble.”

Han Sooyoung clicked her tongue as though she found him pathetic, flipping a coin with her finger.

Yoo Joonghyuk answered coldly.

“This is none of your concern.”

“Why wouldn’t it be? We’re companions.”

“Companions?”

Yoo Joonghyuk’s lips twisted.

“You are not.”

“You think you can say whatever you want······? Hey, I don’t care if you’re the protagonist······!”

“Sooyoung-ssi.”

The companions who had rushed over belatedly tried to stop her. Han Sooyoung pressed a hand to her forehead and muttered,

“Haa······. Kim Dokja and Yoo Joonghyuk are seriously going to put me in an early grave······.”

“Anna Croft must be eliminated here.”

“Well, I don’t think Kim Dokja would want that.”

“This has nothing to do with Kim Dokja—”

“You just want to get one over on that woman, right?”

Yoo Joonghyuk paused and looked at Han Sooyoung. She watched him briefly, then turned toward the auction house entrance.

“I’ve got a good idea. Interested?”

An item rested in Han Sooyoung’s hand.

Yoo Joonghyuk’s eyes wavered.

“That is······?”

“I sneaked it out of Kim Dokja’s coat earlier.”

A mischievous smile formed on her lips.

“Let’s test just how far a Prophet’s ‘prophecies’ go.”

The auction house was one of the few places to obtain Star Relic-grade items difficult to find in the ‘Dokkaebi Bag’ or ordinary ‘exchanges.’ And there were several items the Prophet ‘Anna Croft’ had to obtain here.

Anna Croft spoke to the constellations from <Olympus> standing behind her.

“There won’t be any problems with security, will there?”

[Of course not. We of <Olympus> have jurisdiction over this auction house, after all. As long as you have our protection, no one in the ‘Context of the Constellations’ will be able to touch you.]

“Thank you.”

When Anna Croft bowed her head, the shadows of the constellations protecting her vanished.

Anna Croft spoke to Selena Kim beside her.

“Let’s go in, then.”

“······Yes.”

Selena Kim answered in a subdued voice.

As they walked down the auction house passage, Anna Croft watched Selena Kim’s expression. Selena Kim, always kind and pleasant to everyone, always smiling, had stopped smiling at some point.

“Selena.”

“Yes.”

In truth, Anna Croft knew very well when it had begun.

The Gourmet Association (美食協).

More precisely, after meeting the ‘Demon King of Salvation.’

“······Never mind.”

The sight of Selena Kim lowering her head and facing forward again.

Though she had ‘foreseen’ it to some extent, Anna Croft felt strangely lonely.

Some futures were impossible to handle properly even when you knew them.

Human emotions, in particular, were like that.

[The 8,611th ‘Constellation Auction’ will now begin!]

But now wasn’t the time to dwell on such things.

Watching the fervor of the constellations and incarnations filling the seats, Anna Croft reaffirmed her resolve. Wherever she looked, there was no ‘Status’ to take lightly.

All of them were enemies she had to kill.

[Our first auction item!]

The auctioneer was a semi-advanced-grade dokkaebi on the platform.

Anna Croft and Selena Kim participated from the seats they had secured in advance. Several items sold in quick succession, and Anna Croft bought some of them.

‘Manticore’s Tooth.’

‘Ancient Dragon Scale Fragment.’

‘Old Yeti Hide.’

Most of her purchases were rare materials. Every item had been confirmed through her [Future Sight], and there wasn’t a single error in her list.

‘I need these items to build a Giant Soldier.’

Some incarnations competed in the bidding, but she’d already confirmed their maximum bids through [Future Sight]. Winning the items posed no difficulty.

Finishing her check of the list, Anna Croft rose.

“I believe that’s more or less everything. Then we should······.”

[Now, we have a special item today!]

The sudden voice from the stage made Anna Croft turn sharply.

Seeing Anna Croft’s reaction, Selena Kim asked,

“What is it?”

“Nothing.”

Her expression stiffening, Anna Croft glared across the auction hall.

[This item is called the ‘Old to New Toad’!]

—Croak, croak.

[Haha, cute, isn’t it? Despite its appearance, this is a ‘Star Relic’-grade item······.]

—Give me an old hou se, I’ll give you a new house. Give me an old house, I’ll gi ve you a new house.

[It can even talk quite well. We haven’t finished appraising this lot yet, but it is certainly of tremendous value—]

‘······There wasn’t an item like that in my ‘prophecy,’ was there?’

She’d already checked the full list of auction items through [Future Sight]. Yet nowhere in the fragments of the future she’d seen had an item like that appeared.

That meant some variable capable of disrupting [Future Sight] had intervened.

Anna Croft glanced toward the constellations of <Olympus>. Some nodded back reassuringly.

Without hesitation, she activated the [Great Demon’s Eyes], focusing them on the stage.

Whiiiiir······.

Her eyes, burning brightly and casting a red light. A moment later, the hidden functions of the ‘Old to New Toad’ appeared in Anna Croft’s vision.

“I have to buy that.”

“······Anna-nim?”

[The opening price is ‘500,000 coins’!]

The moment the dokkaebi finished speaking, Anna Croft placed a bid.
